What takes the shell of a well or box foundation down into the depth?
Its own weight, while the soil is removed from inside
The reinforced concrete shell sinks under its own weight, while the “clamshell” grab removes the soil from inside – and from under the cutting edge. Buoyancy works against it.
What is the typical size of well foundations?
The well foundation supports columns and walls at discrete points: Ø 0.8–3.0 m, 4–8 m long; at the top they are tied together by a reinforced concrete grillage or slab.
How can the shell friction of a well be reduced?
With bentonite slurry or single-sized rounded gravel, or with a shoulder offset
Because of the shoulder offset and the tapered shape, the cutting edge cuts a larger hole than the shell; thixotropic slurry or rolling gravel can be placed in the gap.
